content.prompt: Find the median of these stem-and-leaf plots. $1\mid 5$ means $15$.

answer.worked:
There are $15$ scores.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Position}&=\frac{15+1}{2}\\\text{Position}&=8\end{align*}$$
The $8^{\mathrm{th}}$ score is $21$, so the median is $21$.

content.prompt: Calculate the summary statistics for each of these stem-and-leaf plots.

answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Range}&=46-0\\\text{Range}&=46\end{align*}$$
$7$ and $19$ each occur twice; every other value occurs once. The modes are $7$ and $19$.

$$\begin{align*}\overline{x}&=\frac{\text{sum of data values}}{\text{number of data values}}\\\overline{x}&=\frac{\begin{gathered}0+7+7+12+15+19+19\\{}+22+23+27+31+42+46\end{gathered}}{13}\\\overline{x}&=\frac{270}{13}\\\overline{x}&\approx20.77\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\text{Position}&=\frac{13+1}{2}\\\text{Position}&=7\end{align*}$$
The seventh value is $19$, so the median is $19$.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Range}&=125-75\\\text{Range}&=50\end{align*}$$
$96$ occurs three times, more often than any other value. The mode is $96$.
$$\begin{align*}\overline{x}&=\frac{\text{sum of data values}}{\text{number of data values}}\\\overline{x}&=\frac{\begin{gathered}75+75+79+79+80+80\\{}+82+96+96+96+97+113\\{}+114+118+121+123+125+125\end{gathered}}{18}\\\overline{x}&=\frac{1774}{18}\\\overline{x}&=98.\dot{5}\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{Position}&=\frac{18+1}{2}\\\text{Position}&=9.5\end{align*}$$
The median is between the ninth and tenth values.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Median}&=\frac{96+96}{2}\\\text{Median}&=96\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\text{Range}&=338-295\\\text{Range}&=43\end{align*}$$
$316$, $318$, $321$ and $333$ each occur twice; every other value occurs once. These four values are the modes.
$$\begin{align*}\overline{x}&=\frac{\text{sum of data values}}{\text{number of data values}}\\\overline{x}&=\frac{\begin{gathered}295+298+309+316+316\\{}+318+318+320+321+321\\{}+324+333+333+338\end{gathered}}{14}\\\overline{x}&=\frac{4460}{14}\\\overline{x}&\approx318.57\end{align*}$$
$$\begin{align*}\text{Position}&=\frac{14+1}{2}\\\text{Position}&=7.5\end{align*}$$
The median is between the seventh and eighth values.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Median}&=\frac{318+320}{2}\\\text{Median}&=319\end{align*}$$

inlines.text: Order the values numerically before finding the median.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Range}&=38-(-26)\\\text{Range}&=64\end{align*}$$
$-19$ and $15$ each occur twice; every other value occurs once. The modes are $-19$ and $15$.
$$\begin{align*}\overline{x}&=\frac{\text{sum of data values}}{\text{number of data values}}\\\overline{x}&=\frac{\begin{gathered}-26+(-20)+(-19)+(-19)\\{}+(-13)+(-4)+7+10+15\\{}+15+20+22+36+38\end{gathered}}{14}\\\overline{x}&=\frac{62}{14}\\\overline{x}&\approx4.43\end{align*}$$
In numerical order, the values are $-26$, $-20$, $-19$, $-19$, $-13$, $-4$, $7$, $10$, $15$, $15$, $20$, $22$, $36$, $38$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Position}&=\frac{14+1}{2}\\\text{Position}&=7.5\end{align*}$$
The median is between the seventh and eighth values.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Median}&=\frac{7+10}{2}\\\text{Median}&=8.5\end{align*}$$

inlines.text: The stem-and-leaf plot represents the daily sales of soft drink from a vending machine.
If the range of sales is 43, what is the value of

spec.sourceRegion: Question 10, plot at the lower right of the question
spec.description: Stem-and-leaf plot with a horizontal rule above the data and a vertical stem/leaf divider. The first leaf is an italic bold N enclosed by a circle. No key is printed.
spec.mathematics: Stems 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 have leaves [N, 5, 5], [4, 7, 7, 9], [0, 5, 8], [2], [0, 7], respectively. The circled N is a single units digit in the value 20 + N.
spec.answerVisibility: All stems, numerical leaves and the circled N remain visible in the student question. The value of N and the supplied answer sentence occur only in answer fields.

answer.worked:
The greatest value is $67$.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Range}&=\text{greatest value}-\text{least value}\\\text{Least value}&=67-43\\\text{Least value}&=24\end{align*}$$

The missing value is $2\mid N=24$, so the missing leaf is $N=4$.

inlines.text: The table shows the numbers of goals scored by a football team in 24 matches.
Complete the table and find the mean number of goals scored.

answer.worked:
The subtotals are the number of goals multiplied by the frequency.

$$\begin{align*}0\times5 &= 0\\1\times8 &= 8\\2\times6 &= 12\\3\times4 &= 12\\4\times1 &= 4\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}\sum f &= 5+8+6+4+1\\\sum f &= 24\\\sum xf &= 0+8+12+12+4\\\sum xf &= 36\\\bar{x} &= \frac{\sum xf}{\sum f}\\\bar{x} &= \frac{36}{24}\\\bar{x} &= 1.5\end{align*}$$

The mean is $1.5$ goals per match.

inlines.text: In a class of 20 students, a poll was taken of the number of cars owned by each family.
The median number of cars owned is 1.5 and the mean number is 1.4 cars.
Fill in the table in such a way to reflect this information.
1 car: 6 students; 2 cars: 8 students; 3 cars: 2 students.
The middle observations are 1 and 2, so 6 students have one car. The total of 28 cars determines the remaining frequencies.

answer.worked:
There are 20 observations, so the median uses positions 10 and 11. Only four observations are zero; a median of $1.5$ therefore requires the middle values to be $1$ and $2$.

Exactly 10 students have at most one car. The number with one car is $10-4=6$.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Total cars}&=20\times1.4\\\text{Total cars}&=28\\\text{Remaining students}&=20-4-6\\\text{Remaining students}&=10\\\text{Remaining cars}&=28-6\\\text{Remaining cars}&=22\end{align*}$$

Ten two-car families would account for $10\times2=20$ cars. The extra $22-20=2$ cars require two three-car families, leaving $10-2=8$ two-car families.

The missing frequencies are $6$, $8$ and $2$ students, respectively.

answer.worked:
For scores $42,43,44,45,46$, the bar heights give cumulative frequencies $5,10,12,12,14$.

Subtract successive cumulative frequencies to obtain the missing frequencies:

$$\begin{align*}\text{Frequency of }44&=12-10\\\text{Frequency of }44&=2\\\text{Frequency of }45&=12-12\\\text{Frequency of }45&=0\\\text{Frequency of }46&=14-12\\\text{Frequency of }46&=2\end{align*}$$

The completed frequencies are $5,5,2,0,2$. Their sum is $14$, agreeing with the final cumulative frequency.

answer.worked:
For scores $84,85,86,87,88$, the column heights give cumulative frequencies $2,4,8,14,16$. The first frequency is $2$. Subtract successive cumulative frequencies for the remaining scores.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Frequency of }84&=2\\\text{Frequency of }85&=4-2\\\text{Frequency of }85&=2\\\text{Frequency of }86&=8-4\\\text{Frequency of }86&=4\\\text{Frequency of }87&=14-8\\\text{Frequency of }87&=6\\\text{Frequency of }88&=16-14\\\text{Frequency of }88&=2\end{align*}$$

Check: $2+2+4+6+2=16$, agreeing with the final cumulative frequency.

answer.worked:
For scores $88,89,90,91,92$, the bar heights give cumulative frequencies $3,9,10,15,20$.

The first frequency is the first cumulative count. Subsequent frequencies are differences between consecutive cumulative counts.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Frequency of }88&=3\\\text{Frequency of }89&=9-3\\\text{Frequency of }89&=6\\\text{Frequency of }90&=10-9\\\text{Frequency of }90&=1\\\text{Frequency of }91&=15-10\\\text{Frequency of }91&=5\\\text{Frequency of }92&=20-15\\\text{Frequency of }92&=5\end{align*}$$

The frequencies $3,6,1,5,5$ sum to $20$, agreeing with the final cumulative frequency.

entries.description:
In a class of 20 students, a poll was taken of the number of cars owned by each family.
The median number of cars owned is 1.5 and the mean number is 1.4 cars.
Fill in the table in such a way to reflect this information.

expectedAnswer.method: There are 20 observations, so the median uses positions 10 and 11. With only four zeros, a median of 1.5 requires these positions to contain 1 and 2 respectively. Exactly ten students therefore have at most one car, giving 10 − 4 = 6 students with one car. Ten students remain. The mean requires 20 × 1.4 = 28 cars altogether. After the six cars belonging to the one-car families, the remaining families account for 22 cars. Ten two-car families would account for 20 cars; the additional two cars require two three-car families, leaving eight two-car families.
